verdict.rationale: Gusto's own 'intelligent payroll automations' gather hours and flag anomalies ahead of payroll, turning payroll into a quick review and sign-off. Its MCP server and CLI let an agent prepare work before each payroll and send a prioritized list of decisions for approval. However, owners must approve every change, and the evidence never shows user-configurable automations that run fully autonomously; the agent pattern relies on an external AI client built on the MCP/CLI. Missing for 10: a documented user-facing way to create and configure custom background automations, evidence of scheduled or triggered autonomous execution without manual sign-off, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
